Create an S3 connection description

Source: R/connection-s3.R
s3.Rd

A connection is scoped to one bucket, the same way smb() is scoped to one share - paths are always relative to that bucket's own key namespace. Support is provided by the s3fs package, used through its underlying S3FileSystem object directly rather than its convenience functions, which share one connection process-wide; a fresh client is built locally for every call, the same way ftp() does. Construction doesn't contact AWS.

Usage

s3(
  bucket,
  aws_access_key_id = NULL,
  aws_secret_access_key = NULL,
  region_name = NULL,
  endpoint = NULL,
  profile_name = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

bucket

Bucket name.

aws_access_key_id

Optional access key id. Maps to the connection's stored username - see set_creds().

aws_secret_access_key

Optional secret access key. When supplied, it is written to the selected keyring credential store and is not retained in the connection.

region_name

Optional AWS region.

endpoint

Optional endpoint URL, for an S3-compatible service other than AWS (e.g. MinIO).

profile_name

Optional named profile to read credentials from, instead of aws_access_key_id/aws_secret_access_key.

...

Backend options, passed through to s3fs::S3FileSystem$new() (for example s3_force_path_style for an S3-compatible service that needs it, or anonymous = TRUE).

Value

A netfs_s3 connection.

See also

Other connection constructors: ftp(), set_creds(), smb(), ssh(), ssh_keygen(), webdav()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
s3("my-bucket", region_name = "us-east-1")
} # }
